- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to account for downward surprise.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak for next 3–5 periods.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75–80), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 3-period moving average of history.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply 1–3% downward bias for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture momentum shifts; use sentiment-weighted average of last 5–7 days to anchor forecast.
